To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the autonomous solar system is capable of covering 78.3 % of the cooling demand for the studied period in Madrid.
the solar air conditioning system can reduce electricity consumption in Spain.

the autonomous solar air-conditioning system was able to provide cooling during most of the hours in the year, and the solar-assisted air-conditioning system with a backup chiller was able to provide most of the cooling demand during the year, but it is not able to provide the cooling demand during peak demand hours.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of a solar-assisted air conditioning system, which is able to provide the cooling demand in the majority of hours of the studied period.

the study of solar air-conditioning installations and their operation under different climatic and operational conditions, as well as the analysis of the energy performance of the solar thermal collector-absorption chiller system in Spain.
the development of solar-powered air conditioning systems that can be used in different climates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
solar thermal systems for air conditioning are still an interesting option in Spain, but only if the solar collector is used to provide heat to an absorption chiller.
the solar-assisted air conditioning system with backup is more suitable for the Spanish climate than the autonomous system, but it is not yet a viable alternative for the market.
solar thermal assisted absorption chillers are not a good solution for air conditioning in Spain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in Spain, the solar assisted system is more effective than the autonomous one.
the solar thermal collector–compression chiller combination is more suitable for air conditioning systems in Spain.
, in the Spanish case study, the autonomous absorption system can cover the cooling demand for most hours of the year.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the solar thermal collector–compression chiller system is more competitive than the absorption chiller in the Spanish climate.
the solar air conditioning systems studied are not competitive in terms of electricity consumption, and that the use of solar energy is limited to a few hours per day.

the solar thermal collector– absorption machine can be an alternative to conventional systems for air conditioning, but it is necessary to have an efficient solar field and a good design of the absorption machine in order to reduce the cost of the installation and the associated electricity consumption.
